title: Canonical forms of even Grassmann matrices
statement: Classify \(L_{p,q}(\Lambda_N)\) under its group of even units, for fixed finite \(N,p,q\), without the simple-body-spectrum hypothesis.
status: As of November 2026, canonical algorithms follow from finite-dimensional algebra similarity and Sergeichuk's linear-matrix-problem theorem. A short Jordan-block classification is a stronger demand; the chapter supplies special cases and a simultaneous-similarity embedding.

title: Even commutants of odd Grassmann matrices
statement: Given arbitrary \(A\in M_n(\Lambda_N^{\bar1})\), describe \(C_{\bar0}(A)\). The notebook specifically highlights \(N=4\).
status: As of November 2026, the literal finite problem is solved by expanding the commutator in Grassmann monomials and computing a finite linear kernel. The chapter gives a complete structural \(n=2,N=4\) result. Any stronger all-size normal-form request is an interpretation not specified in the manuscript; no global openness or novelty claim is made.

title: Describe projective bundles by finite exterior modules
statement: Describe algebraic vector bundles on complex projective space by proper finite graded exterior-algebra modules, up to addition of free modules.
status: Established by BGG in 1978; the 1979 occurrence is exposition. Instanton bundles require extra reality and twistor-line conditions.

title: Explicit maps in the BGG and Beilinson constructions
statement: Construct actual differentials from finite sheaf data, not just the terms of the associated monad or exterior resolution.
status: Developed explicitly by Eisenbud--Fløystad--Schreyer, preprint 2001, publication 2003; see Theorem 6.1 and the construction preceding it.

title: A Grassmannian counterpart of the projective-space linear model
statement: Construct a finite algebraic or homogeneous-bundle model for \(D^b(\operatorname{Coh}\operatorname{Gr}(k,n))\) over \(\mathbb C\).
status: Resolved in the reconstructed derived-category sense by Kapranov, 1984/1985 and the fuller 1988 Theorem 3.4. This does not classify every bundle by a finite list of invariants.

title: The two-dimensional energy representation
statement: Is the ordinary energy representation of \(C^\infty_c(X,G)\) irreducible for every connected smooth surface \(X\), compact semisimple \(G\), and invariant positive covariance data?
status: As of November 2026, a root/covariance inequality gives irreducibility (Wallach 1987, Theorem 6.2). The claimed all-dimensional proof by Shimada has an explicitly documented gap. No unrestricted solution was verified in targeted searches; this is a bounded literature-status conclusion, not an assertion of exhaustive current openness.

title: Universality of the difference-curve resonance construction
statement: Does every regular local two-dimensional three-wave dispersion law with infinitely many independent collision invariants admit the difference-curve parametrization on compatible resonance branches? This reconstructs the immediately preceding infinitely-many-first-integrals programme; it is not the earlier, broader request for one additional invariant.
status: As of November 2026, Balk--Ferapontov's 1994 publication explicitly gives a classification of three-wave interactions with infinitely many invariants. Its full theorem was not retrieved, so exact local and branch hypotheses are unverified. The one-extra-invariant reading is distinct: finite-invariant examples were announced in 1991 and their uniqueness is discussed in the 1998 web-geometry development and Balk2014, Sec.2.1. This is a developed historical question with partial publication matching, not a claim of current openness.

title: Local abelianization of regular first-class constraints
statement: Given independent first-class constraints defining a regular coisotropic submanifold, can local canonical coordinates and an invertible change of constraint generators make all constraint brackets zero? This specifies the local reading of the notebook's question about constant structure functions.
status: As of November 2026 the stated local regular version is affirmative. The notebook does not specify the allowed transformations or any global quantifier; it must not be converted into a universal global abelianization conjecture. Dirac's generator equivalence is older; the constructive 1995 preprint/1996 article is a later explicit treatment.

title: Continuum confinement and the static potential
statement:
For four-dimensional continuum pure \(SU(N)\) Yang--Mills theory at zero temperature, with fixed finite \(N\ge2\) and external fundamental static sources, establish a well-defined subtracted static potential with positive asymptotic string tension:
\[
\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{V(r)}r=\tau>0.
\]
There are no dynamical fundamental quarks in this formulation. Occurrence 1979-480.3 specializes to \(SU(3)\). Occurrence 1979-482.14 returns to the general confinement goal and proposes normalized large-rank loop equations as a route; that limiting method is not identified with the fixed-rank statement. The stronger constant-width flux-tube hypothesis is excluded from this problem identity.
status: As of 10 November 2026, the verified results are partial. Wilson's strong-coupling lattice area law \citep[Secs.~IV and VI]{wilson1974confinement} and the controlled large-rank lattice expansion \citep[Theorem~3.1 and Corollaries~3.2--3.3]{chatterjee2015string} do not provide the asserted continuum proof. With light dynamical quarks, string breaking changes the asymptotic static-energy question \citep[Sec.~4]{bulava2019string}. The continuum existence-and-mass-gap problem and confinement are separately stated in \citet[Sec.~5]{jaffewitten2000yangmills}; the former is still listed as unsolved by \citet{clay2026yangmills}. The reused older identifier follows the static-potential goal, while the distinct proposed methods and physical regimes remain explicit.

title: Kazhdan--Lusztig multiplicity and cohomological conjectures
statement: For a regular integral block of category \(\mathcal O\), recover Verma composition multiplicities and the graded Ext dimensions from the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials, with the precise antidominant indexing in occurrences 1979-483.6--7.
status: As of 10 November 2026: solved. The independent geometric proofs circulated by the 1980 Toru\'n meeting and were published in 1981; see \citet[pp.~43--44]{brylinski1981differential}, \citet{brylinskikashiwara1981holonomic}, and \citet{beilinsonbernstein1981localisation}. This status concerns complex characteristic-zero regular integral category \(\mathcal O\), not unrestricted modular analogues.
